title: When Workers Were Paid in Beer
hook: 5,000 years ago in Sumeria, money didn't exist—laborers were paid in gallons of fermenting beer.

scenes.text: Long before coins or banknotes were invented, the ancient Sumerian city-states built the world's first civilization powered entirely by beer.
scenes.imagePrompt: Towering mudbrick ziggurat temple rising above the fertile green river plain of Mesopotamia at dawn. 2D flat cartoon illustration, thick dark outlines, warm muted palette, hand-painted textures, vertical 9:16, no people in the foreground, no text, no logos
scenes.voicedText: Long before coins or banknotes were invented, the ancient Sumerian city-states built the world's first civilization powered entirely by beer.

scenes.text: Mesopotamian beer wasn't like modern lager: it was a thick, sour, nutrient-dense porridge brewed from twice-baked barley bread called 'bappir'.
scenes.imagePrompt: Earthenware brewing vats with malted barley grain, dried loaves of bappir bread, and ceramic measuring bowls. 2D flat cartoon illustration, thick dark outlines, warm muted palette, hand-painted textures, vertical 9:16, no people in the foreground, no text, no logos
scenes.voicedText: Mesopotamian beer wasn't like modern lager: it was a thick, sour, nutrient-dense porridge brewed from twice-baked barley bread called 'bappir'.

scenes.text: Because river water was full of dangerous parasites, boiling the mash made beer the safest hydrating drink available.
scenes.imagePrompt: Clay jug of frothy golden beer with long hollow reed drinking straws resting on an adobe table. 2D flat cartoon illustration, thick dark outlines, warm muted palette, hand-painted textures, vertical 9:16, no people in the foreground, no text, no logos
scenes.voicedText: Because river water was full of dangerous parasites, boiling the mash made beer the safest hydrating drink available.

scenes.text: Temple records on clay tablets reveal standard wages: laborers received two liters a day, while senior officials received five liters daily.
scenes.imagePrompt: Cuneiform clay tablet inscribed with reed stylus tally marks showing the beer jar pictograph symbol. 2D flat cartoon illustration, thick dark outlines, warm muted palette, hand-painted textures, vertical 9:16, no people in the foreground, no text, no logos
scenes.voicedText: Temple records on clay tablets reveal standard wages: laborers received two liters a day, while senior officials received five liters daily.

scenes.text: Because chaff floated on top, drinkers used long bent bronze and reed straws to sip clean brew from the bottom of communal jars.
